records.rationale: Complete permission/proc-mode patch read against positive GrapheneOS consumer evidence. ActivityManagerService constructs LowMemDetector; JNI requests 1,000,000-us memory windows, libpsi opens/writes the proc node, Zygote system_server capability list lacks SYS_RESOURCE and policy expressly forbids it while allowing proc_pressure_mem writes. Native unprivileged 2-second-only policy would reject these monitors. Retain ACK compile-time SELinux-default relaxation and proc default mode 0444 (mode 0 expands in proc_create_reg); Android init changes memory node ownership/mode to system:system 0666. This intentionally removes CAP_SYS_RESOURCE gating for all otherwise permitted proc/cgroup PSI writers when the config is enabled, regardless of runtime SELinux enforcement. Native size/range/one-trigger-per-fd and lifetime protections remain. Security cost is access to short-window SCHED_FIFO-low polling and extra work; rely on actual file/LSM policy, not an assumed runtime check. No global sandbox-access proof or resource-exhaustion bound claimed.

security: Compatibility requires one-second polling without SYS_RESOURCE for system_server. ACK relaxation affects all permitted writers, including cgroup nodes, and selects PSI_POLL instead of PSI_AVGS. It is a compile-time DEFAULT_SECURITY_SELINUX test, not proof that SELinux is active/enforcing; permissive/disabled policy broadens exposure. A user able to write a node can request short-window polling and consume kernel/RT worker resources. Native parameter bounds and lifetime fixes remain; no measured overhead, runtime policy compilation or exhaustive app-domain access proof. Default proc mode becomes 0444, but Android init explicitly chmods memory to 0666, leaving LSM enforcement material.
consumers: Positive supplied source evidence: ActivityManagerService -> LowMemDetector -> JNI -> libpsi write of 1s windows. Zygote capability list lacks SYS_RESOURCE; system_server policy neverallows it and allows memory-pressure rw. lmkd also uses PSI but its service already has SYS_RESOURCE, so it does not itself establish necessity of the bypass.
uncertainty: Exact PSI vendor hook consumers unconfirmed. Actual SDK boot command line, SELinux enforcement and memory-pressure notification behavior are not runtime verified. The old compile-time per-cgroup switch is superseded by native configuration, not evidence that cgroup pressure is unused.
